note: Both the sensitising EGFR mutations (2004) and the T790M resistance mutation (2005) were found in patients first and then recapitulated in cells; the one prospective model prediction in this context, osimertinib's activity against T790M, held, while the cell-defined T790M exposure target for irreversible quinazolines did not.
label: NSCLC (EGFR TKIs)

engagement.note: Cells expressing the mutations found in responders were more gefitinib-sensitive; the clinic informed the model, so no prospective prediction existed yet.
engagement.short: Mutant receptors found in responders drug-sensitive in vitro
engagement.quote: In vitro, EGFR mutants demonstrated enhanced tyrosine kinase activity in response to epidermal growth factor and increased sensitivity to inhibition by gefitinib.
engagement.judgement: Lynch 2004 (and Paez 2004 in Science the same day) compares model and patients in one paper, but in the patient-to-model direction (mutations sequenced from responders, then tested in cells); a retrodiction is not scored as 'same'.

engagement.model: T790M-mutant cells (H1975) and L858R/T790M transgenic mice
engagement.note: H1975/T790M cells and mice said osimertinib engages T790M-mutant EGFR while sparing wild-type; T790M-positive tumours responded 61%, T790M-negative 21%.
engagement.quote: Among 127 patients with centrally confirmed EGFR T790M who could be evaluated for response, the response rate was 61% (95% CI, 52 to 70).
engagement.judgement: Cross 2014 (10.1158/2159-8290.CD-14-0337) published the cell/xenograft/transgenic prediction, including wild-type sparing, before AURA's T790M-stratified result (abstract-level reading; Cross 2014 also carried 2 early patient cases). T790M itself was not predicted: Kobayashi 2005 (10.1056/NEJMoa044238) found it in a relapsing patient and only then showed resistance in modelling and cells.

dose.note: H1975 cells said irreversible quinazolines (neratinib, later afatinib) inhibit T790M EGFR at concentrations the drugs reach in culture; no patient exposure comparison yet.
dose.quote: These inhibitors also show effective inhibition of signaling by T790M-mutant EGFR and killing of NSCLC cells with the T790M mutation.

dose.note: Wild-type-EGFR diarrhoea forced neratinib from 320 to 240 mg; exposure never reached the cell-defined T790M-inhibitory level; no T790M patient responded.
dose.short: Diarrhoea capped dose; no T790M responses
dose.quote: Neratinib had low activity in patients with prior benefit from TKIs and in TKI-naive patients, potentially because of insufficient bioavailability from diarrhea-imposed dose limitation.
dose.judgement: Scored as a dose failure, not an efficacy failure, because the paper itself attributes the miss to diarrhoea-limited exposure (the abstract also states 'No patients with known T790M responded'). Afatinib's pivotal paper (Li 2008, 10.1038/onc.2008.109) made the same cell/mouse claim and LUX-Lung 1 (Miller 2012, 10.1016/S1470-2045(12)70087-6: ORR 7%, OS HR 1.08 vs placebo, 87% diarrhoea) fits the same pattern; quote has 'naive' for the abstract's 'naïve'.

dose.model: Mutant-selective cell panel and L858R/T790M mice (osimertinib)
dose.note: Cross 2014 predicted T790M inhibition below wild-type-toxic exposure; AURA found no dose-limiting toxicity at 20-240 mg and 61% T790M response across doses.
dose.short: Mutant-selective window: no DLT, T790M hit
dose.quote: Among 31 patients enrolled in the dose-escalation cohorts, no dose-limiting toxic effects occurred at the doses evaluated.
dose.reason: Selectivity window held; quinazoline exposure did not
dose.judgement: Status moves contra to same because the best model changed (H1975 potency alone to a mutant-versus-wild-type selectivity window with mouse PK/PD); if the atlas treats contra as sticky per model system, keep contra. The FDA clinical pharmacology review for osimertinib was not read; abstract-level only.

efficacy.note: Mutation-bearing cells were gefitinib-hypersensitive, but the mutations were found by sequencing responders, so the model explained the clinic rather than predicting it.
efficacy.short: Cells explained responders; no prospective test
efficacy.quote: Screening for such mutations in lung cancers may identify patients who will have a response to gefitinib.

efficacy.model: EGFR-mutant cell lines and EGFR-mutant transgenic mice
efficacy.note: First prospective test of the model-defined population: 16 mutation-positive patients, 75% response, PFS 9.7 months; IPASS 2009 then randomised it (HR 0.48).
efficacy.quote: The overall response rate in these patients was 75% (95% CI, 54% to 96%), and the disease control rate was 88% (95% CI, 71% to 100%).
efficacy.judgement: Inoue 2006 is the first published prospective comparison, so the year is 2006 rather than IPASS (Mok 2009, 10.1056/NEJMoa0810699; mutation-positive PFS HR 0.48, mutation-negative HR 2.85). Transgenic mice (Politi 2006, 10.1101/gad.1417406) predicted erlotinib regression the same year, still after the clinical observation.

efficacy.note: T790M mice said afatinib alone fails, afatinib plus cetuximab shrinks tumours; LUX-Lung 1 gave 7% response, the combination 32% in T790M-positive patients.
efficacy.short: Mouse flagged afatinib alone; combo matched
efficacy.quote: Among 126 patients, objective response rate (overall 29%) was comparable in T790M-positive and T790M-negative tumors (32% vs. 25%; P = 0.341).
efficacy.reason: Mouse flagged afatinib alone; combination matched
efficacy.judgement: The flag is Regales 2009 (10.1172/JCI38746: 'only the combination of both agents together induced dramatic shrinkage of erlotinib-resistant tumors harboring the T790M mutation'), published before LUX-Lung 1 (Miller 2012: ORR 7%, OS HR 1.08; not T790M-selected). But afatinib's own pivotal paper (Li 2008) claimed regression in the same mice and was not borne out; that miss is booked under dose. A stricter reading makes efficacy contra from 2012. Mouse 'dramatic shrinkage' versus 29% ORR / 4.7-month PFS is a directional, not quantitative, match. Osimertinib (AURA 2015) matched the same cells/mice without changing status.

safety.note: Nonclinical toxicology in the label is silent on lung injury; fatal acute interstitial pneumonia appeared within months of launch, 1.3% overall, higher in Japan.
safety.quote: We assessed four patients who had non-small cell lung cancer causing severe acute interstitial pneumonia in association with gefitinib.
safety.judgement: The comparison is a juxtaposition: the 2015 Iressa label (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/206995s000lbl.pdf) gives ILD in 1.3% of 2,462 patients with 3 deaths and a >2-fold exposure-ILD relation, while its nonclinical section reports only carcinogenicity and fertility findings; the 2003 FDA pharmacology review was not read, so the animal silence is inferred from the label. Osimertinib's wild-type-sparing prediction of less rash/diarrhoea did hold, but its label still warns of ILD (not fetched here), so the status stays contra.
